newsitem.title: UK: Emirates no plans to boost future UK-HK cargo role.
newsitem.headline: Emirates no plans to boost future UK-HK cargo role.

text.p: Emirates said it is making no special plans to increase its share of the UK-Hong Kong air cargo, market after the colony is handed back by Britain to China on July 1.
At present, UK-HK is a cabotage route, supposedly restricted mainly to British carriers, a practice that will end following the Chinese takeover, say industry observers.

Other airlines have for a number of years been serving the market via an intermediate point, usually their home base, and Emirates' UK cargo market controller Jaqui Evans said the Dubai government-owned carrier was one of these.

"Yes, we have been serving the route unofficially. But before we start openly selling UK-Hong Kong -- producing rate lists and sending out mailshots -- we want to see how the market goes," she told a news briefing.
The airline's UK and Ireland general manager, Mohamed Qasim Al Ali, forecast that Hong Kong would continue to grow in general economic and air passenger and freight terms after the handover.
"The Chinese are not that stupid as to kill the golden goose," he said.
